content:
SAMUEL ACHTERBERG-OSEI
Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with experience designing and operating Azure environments, building Terraform infrastructure and automating deployments. Background includes Azure landing zone networking, AKS operations, security baselines and leading a 60-server migration to Azure. Experienced with Windows and Linux systems, PowerShell and Azure DevOps pipelines.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: Azure VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure AD / Entra ID, Azure Monitor, Azure Migrate, VMware
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Bicep, Ansible, PowerShell, Bash, Azure DevOps Pipelines
Containers: Docker, Kubernetes, AKS, Helm
Systems and networking: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Active Directory, Microsoft 365 administration, TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls
Security: Azure Firewall, private endpoints, MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing, backups
Other programming: Python scripting; Go for Terratest tests

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V.
Mar 2025–Present
- Operate an Azure estate of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions as part of a three-person cloud team.
- Built Terraform modules for landing zone networking, including hub-spoke VNets, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and a nightly infrastructure drift detection job.
- Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS. Deployment frequency increased from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
- Operate AKS clusters, including upgrades, node pools and ingress; application manifests are owned by developers.

Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed
Sep 2022–Jan 2024
- Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5–40 employees.
- Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for security baselines, including MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing and backups.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Jan 2014–Feb 2020
- Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
- Led the 2019 lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate, with cutover over six weekends and no unplanned downtime.
- Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
- Provided second-line escalation for networking and Active Directory issues.

Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Aug 2011–Dec 2013

CAREER BREAKS AND DEVELOPMENT
Feb 2024–Feb 2025: Studied Terraform, built a Proxmox homelab and completed a part-time online cloud bootcamp in English in December 2024. Earned the Terraform Associate certification in 2025.

Mar 2020–Aug 2022: Full-time family caregiving. Maintained Azure knowledge and provided unpaid IT support to church and family.

EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College | 2011

CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104)
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003), 2025

LANGUAGES
Dutch: Native | English: Fluent | Twi: Spoken

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear cloud/infrastructure focus, relevant quantified achievements, consistent reverse-chronological experience, and transparent treatment of career breaks. The strongest evidence includes operating approximately 400 Azure VMs and 12 AKS clusters, building Terraform landing-zone modules, automating deployment pipelines for 15 applications, and leading a 60-server Azure migration with no unplanned downtime. The document is professional and easy to scan. Its main limitation is that some role-relevant concepts—systems architecture, technical leadership, and stakeholder management—are implied rather than stated explicitly.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, recognizable technology names, quantified achievements, and ATS-friendly bullet structure. It should parse reliably and has a high AI/ATS screening probability for Azure, Terraform, Kubernetes, AKS, infrastructure automation, networking, Linux, virtual machines, and security. Alignment would improve modestly by using the job description's supported terminology more directly, such as “infrastructure as code,” “cloud environment design and operation,” “Azure landing zone architecture,” “network design,” “system design,” and “technical leadership.” Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, or IoT keywords because they are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for hands-on Azure infrastructure engineering, cloud operations, Terraform, networking, security awareness, Linux, and virtual machines. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background even though AWS is preferred. The landing-zone work, private endpoints, Azure Firewall, private DNS, VNet peering, drift detection, AKS operations, and Azure DevOps pipelines align well with the platform reliability and security aspects of the role. The candidate's material shows gaps in Terragrunt, mTLS/certificate management, SSL/TLS, AWS, IoT/automotive or remote-device integration, and a backend/full-stack background. Stakeholder management with external manufacturers and explicit end-to-end technical proposal leadership are also not evidenced. These are capability gaps or unproven areas, not defects that can be corrected by wording alone. The CV does show relevant adjacent experience through technical ownership of migration, infrastructure modules, deployment automation, and operational reliability.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, change “experience designing and operating Azure environments, building Terraform infrastructure and automating deployments” to “experience designing, building and operating Azure cloud environments, developing Terraform infrastructure as code and automating deployments.” This uses the job description's terminology without adding unsupported experience.
2. In the Professional Summary, add “Azure landing zone architecture, network design, systems administration and practical cloud security” after the existing reference to Azure landing zones. These terms are supported by the documented hub-spoke networking, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, Azure Migrate, MFA, conditional access and server administration work.
3. Under Cloud Engineer at Havenstad Logistics, change “Built Terraform modules for landing zone networking” to “Designed and built Terraform infrastructure-as-code modules for Azure landing-zone network architecture.” This more clearly presents the work as cloud design and systems architecture while remaining truthful.
4. Under Systems Administrator at Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, change “Led the 2019 lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate” to “Planned and led the 2019 lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed the cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.” The candidate portfolio supports the added “planned” wording and this gives stronger evidence of technical leadership and delivery ownership.
5. In the Technical Skills section, change “Infrastructure as code and automation” to “Infrastructure as code, cloud automation and deployment” and retain Terraform, Bicep, Ansible, PowerShell, Bash and Azure DevOps Pipelines beneath it. This improves keyword alignment without implying Terragrunt experience.
6. In the Cloud Engineer bullets, retain the quantified deployment outcome, but change “Deployment frequency increased from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications” to “Improved deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.” This makes the achievement more direct and outcome-oriented.
